ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a curve of the potential energy between two hydrogen atoms changing with internuclear distance; the vertical axis is labeled Potential Energy, and the horizontal axis is labeled Internuclear Distance. At a very small distance, the curve has very high potential energy, then drops to form a deep potential well, then gradually rises again and approaches the zero potential energy level. Mark A is at the high-potential-energy place on the left, B is on the descending segment near the zero-potential-energy area, C is located at the lowest point of the potential well, and D is in the flat area on the right near zero potential energy. Reasoning: The most stable state of the molecule corresponds to the position of lowest potential energy, because the system is most stable when it is at the lowest potential energy. The lowest point in the figure is C, so the most stable H2 molecular state is represented by Point C.

method.method_draft: First describe the image as a potential-energy curve versus internuclear distance with a deep well; identify which labeled point is lowest on the curve. Then apply the rule that the most stable molecular state is the state with the lowest potential energy. Since point C is at the bottom of the well, select Point C.

method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中是两个氢原子之间势能随核间距离变化的势能曲线。纵轴标为 Potential Energy (kJ/mol)，横轴标为 Internuclear Distance (nm)。曲线在很短距离处势能很高，经过标记 A 附近向下，经过 B 附近继续下降，然后在一个势能最低的谷底处标记为 C，之后随距离增大上升并在右侧 D 附近接近零势能水平。
